Anomaly comparisons

Results

To understand whether there was a relationship between the output of the Index and the calculated mean monthly strength values, multiple linear regression models were calculated.

Full model

# data wrangling

# Extract data sources
raw_data <- readRDS(file.path("var", "raw_data_list.rds"))

raw_strength_data <- raw_data$raw_strength_data
raw_index_data <- raw_data$raw_index_data

# combine raw data values

comb_raw_data <- raw_strength_data %>% 
  inner_join(raw_index_data, by = "date") %>%  # inner join to remove NA values
  mutate(
    month = month(date) # extract month value
  ) %>% 
  rename(cop_strength = mean_vel)

# pivot longer for model

comb_raw_data_long <- comb_raw_data %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(cop_strength, eac_cci),
               names_to = "data_source",
               values_to = "value")

head(comb_raw_data_long)
# A tibble: 6 × 4
  date                month data_source     value
  <dttm>              <dbl> <chr>           <dbl>
1 2011-03-01 00:00:00     3 cop_strength  0.226  
2 2011-03-01 00:00:00     3 eac_cci      -0.0519 
3 2011-05-01 00:00:00     5 cop_strength  0.0925 
4 2011-05-01 00:00:00     5 eac_cci      -0.110  
5 2011-07-01 00:00:00     7 cop_strength  0.00652
6 2011-07-01 00:00:00     7 eac_cci      -0.0420

data_source is whether the values come from the output of the EAC CCI Index calculation or are the Mean monthly strength values from the Copernicus Global Ocean Physics Reanalysis https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030/description.

ggplot(data = comb_raw_data_long, aes(x = data_source, y = value)) +
  geom_jitter(data = comb_raw_data_long,
             aes(x = data_source, y = value), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3)
# create the model

raw_data_model <- lm(value ~ data_source + month + month:data_source, data = comb_raw_data_long)

summary(raw_data_model)

Call:
lm(formula = value ~ data_source + month + month:data_source, 
    data = comb_raw_data_long)

Residuals:
      Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
-0.222944 -0.065094 -0.002974  0.067237  0.302831 

Coefficients:
                          Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)               0.082429   0.033677   2.448 0.015933 *  
data_sourceeac_cci        0.035162   0.047627   0.738 0.461893    
month                     0.006220   0.004287   1.451 0.149621    
data_sourceeac_cci:month -0.021367   0.006063  -3.524 0.000616 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.09806 on 112 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.3411,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.3234 
F-statistic: 19.32 on 3 and 112 DF,  p-value: 3.619e-10
gglm(raw_data_model)
plot_predictions(raw_data_model, condition = 'data_source') +
  geom_jitter(data = comb_raw_data_long,
             aes(x = data_source, y = value), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3)

A multiple linear regression was conducted to examine the effects of the data source, month, and their interaction on the resulting values.

The overall model was statistically significant, F(3, 112) = 19.32, p < 0.001, explaining approximately 34.1% of the variance in the dependent variable (R² = 0.341, adjusted R² = 0.323).

The interaction between data source and month was statistically significant (β = -0.0214, t = -3.52, p < .001), indicating that the effect of month on value differed depending on the data source.

Residuals were symmetrically distributed with a standard error of 0.0981, ranging from -0.223 to 0.303, suggesting that the model does not under or overfit.

# drop the interaction term
raw_data_model2 <- lm(value ~ data_source + month, data = comb_raw_data_long)

summary(raw_data_model2)

Call:
lm(formula = value ~ data_source + month, data = comb_raw_data_long)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-0.21112 -0.07598 -0.02006  0.07770  0.28025 

Coefficients:
                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)         0.159975   0.026752   5.980 2.67e-08 ***
data_sourceeac_cci -0.119930   0.019106  -6.277 6.58e-09 ***
month              -0.004463   0.003181  -1.403    0.163    
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.1029 on 113 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.268, Adjusted R-squared:  0.255 
F-statistic: 20.68 on 2 and 113 DF,  p-value: 2.215e-08
gglm(raw_data_model2)
plot_predictions(raw_data_model2, condition = 'data_source') +
  geom_jitter(data = comb_raw_data_long,
             aes(x = data_source, y = value), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3)

A second regression was conducted to remove the effect of the interaction between data source and month.

This model was also statistically significant, F(2, 113) = 20.68, p < 0.001, explaining approximately 26.8 % variance in the dependent variable (R² = 0.268, adjusted R² = 0.255).

  • The intercept was statistically significant (β = 0.1599, t = 5.980, p < 0.001).

  • The main effect of data source was statistically significant (β = 0.1199, t = -6.277, p < 0.001).

  • The main effect of month was not significant (β = 0.0044, t = -1.403, p = 0.163).

Residuals were symmetrically distributed with a standard error of 0.1029, ranging from -0.211 to 0.280.

# compare the two models 

anova(raw_data_model, raw_data_model2, test = "F")
Analysis of Variance Table

Model 1: value ~ data_source + month + month:data_source
Model 2: value ~ data_source + month
  Res.Df    RSS Df Sum of Sq      F    Pr(>F)    
1    112 1.0769                                  
2    113 1.1963 -1  -0.11941 12.419 0.0006164 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

To assess whether the interaction between month and the source of data significantly improves the model fit, an analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted comparing two nested models:

  • Model 1: included main effects of data_source and month, as well as their interaction (month:data_source).

  • Model 2: included only the main effects of data_source and month.

The comparison revealed that Model 1 provided a significantly better fit to the data than Model 2, F(1, 112) = 12.42, p < .001. This indicates that the seasonal cycles were different, and that including the interaction term significantly improves the model’s explanatory power.

Comparing the anomalies

As the climatologies had a significant correlation between them, a linear regression was calculated between the anomalies to model the relationship.

# load libraries

library(tidyverse)

# Extract data sources
combined_anomaly_data <- readRDS(file.path("var", "combined_anomalies.rds"))

head(combined_anomaly_data)
# A tibble: 6 × 3
  trip_month          index_anom strength_anom
  <dttm>                   <dbl>         <dbl>
1 2011-03-01 00:00:00     0.0959        0.0710
2 2011-05-01 00:00:00     0.0210       -0.0216
3 2011-07-01 00:00:00    -0.0795       -0.0989
4 2011-12-01 00:00:00     0.0444        0.0191
5 2012-04-01 00:00:00     0.0674       -0.107 
6 2012-09-01 00:00:00    -0.0850        0.0334
# model to compare the anomalies of the Index and the Strength values
anomaly_model <- lm(index_anom ~ strength_anom, data = combined_anomaly_data)

summary(anomaly_model)

Call:
lm(formula = index_anom ~ strength_anom, data = combined_anomaly_data)

Residuals:
      Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
-0.100317 -0.069935 -0.006883  0.060471  0.107614 

Coefficients:
               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)   -0.006099   0.009075  -0.672    0.504
strength_anom  0.100453   0.128095   0.784    0.436

Residual standard error: 0.0691 on 56 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.01086,   Adjusted R-squared:  -0.006801 
F-statistic: 0.615 on 1 and 56 DF,  p-value: 0.4362
gglm(anomaly_model)
plot_predictions(anomaly_model, condition = 'strength_anom') +
  geom_point(data = combined_anomaly_data,
             aes(x = strength_anom, y = index_anom))

The combined_anomalies2 tibble has 2 key variables:

  1. eac_cci_clim : The Index anomalies

  2. strength_anom : The strength anomalies calculated from the Copernicus data

The model was not statistically significant, F(1, 56) = 0.615, p = 0.436, and explained only a small proportion of the variance in the Index anomalies (R² = 0.011, adjusted R² = -0.007).

The slope coefficient for strength anomaly was not statistically significant (β = 0.1005, t = 0.784, p = 0.436), indicating that changes in strength anomaly did not significantly predict changes in EAC CCI climate anomaly.

The residuals were approximately symmetrically distributed, with a standard error of 0.0691, and ranged from -0.100 to 0.108.
